races.title: State House, District 51
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: April Montgomery
cands.bio: Independent (unaffiliated) elected to the North Carolina House for District 51 in 2026. Chief development officer at a Chapel Hill energy storage company. Co-owns a historic commercial building restoration firm and founded a sustainability consultancy, sold in 2019. Lives in Sanford.

endorsements.text: North Carolina Forward Party, plus voter-guide recommendations from Better Future NC (Cam Pruette), Bull City Anna's Voting Group, Fair Map Fight Club and Imani's Pix.

cands.gaps: We could not find where she grew up, or the city in Florida where she was born. We found no documented actions in office. We found no stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor purchases of land and homes, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns or abortion. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no independent news reporting about her. Details of her energy company employer and her business ventures come only from a Wikipedia page, with no primary source.

local.label: Roots 55: Wikipedia says she was born in Florida and moved to North Carolina in 1999, about 27 years before the 2026 election, and her campaign site cites 22 years living in the district.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Chief development officer at an energy storage company, co-owner of a historic building restoration firm, and founder of a sustainability consultancy sold to a national environmental firm in 2019. She holds a master's degree in urban and regional planning. She has not held elected office.
qual.why: Business ownership and management and a planning degree fit the middle band. She has no prior legislative service and no law or budget career that can be shown. Board chairs and advisory seats are not counted.

cands.name: Charles M. Taylor
cands.bio: Republican candidate for North Carolina House District 51 in 2026. He won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 54.2% of the vote over Sherry Womack. Ballotpedia lists no occupation, offices held or biography for him.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Charles Taylor was born or raised, when he came to North Carolina, or his career and education. We found no record of any elected office he has held. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, so we have no stated positions on data centers, property taxes, development, immigration, guns, abortion, schools, policing or campaign money. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him. We found no news coverage or controversies about him. The only page available was a short Ballotpedia profile.
